title: Beni Mellal city and foothills on 8 Oct 2026
summary: On 8 Oct 2026 the radar shows Beni Mellal city and its foothills inside a 6 km circle, with built-up land on 12.2% and trees, shrub and rugged slopes on 52.5%. This date carries a flag for a backscatter shift, so its values are less reliable than those of an unflagged date.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: Built-up land reaches 7.3 dB in HH, and the circle averages -0.58 dB in HH and -13.03 dB in HV. Every type is bright on this date, smooth bare ground included, at -13.18 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Built-up land, 13.75 km2, keeps the lowest HV:HH ratio, -17.56 dB, from walls that bounce the pulse straight back. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes give HV of -12.24 dB from leaves and branches. Rough dry ground and fields, 27.3%, sit at -8.63 dB in HH. Changing fields cover 5.4 km2 at -14.15 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: One flag applies: backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median, a possible processing offset or widespread wet conditions. Possible cause: a processing offset in this product; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: rain wetting soil and walls; rain records would check it. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.
